user_reviews.Description:
This place is huge and features a beautiful Japanese-style garden. It was super crowded when I visited, likely because it coincided with the Chiang Mai University graduation. The crowd was a mix of teenagers and office workers, so it was quite bustling and not very peaceful. Luckily, my group managed to find a seat just in time!

There is an 80 THB entrance fee, but you can use the ticket as a discount for food and drinks inside.

The prices are standard for a cafe, and everything tasted good. The staff were friendly and provided great service. Since it was so busy, the drinks were served in order, so you might have to wait a bit. Overall, a lovely spot—just be prepared for the crowd on busy days!

user_reviews.Name: Sutrisno Yao
user_reviews.Description:
The Baristro x Ping River is a masterclass in blending industrial design with the natural serenity of Chiang Mai’s riverfront. From the moment you step inside, the raw concrete walls and minimalist wooden accents create an atmosphere that feels both modern and incredibly welcoming. The expansive glass windows offer a stunning view of the Ping River, making it the perfect sanctuary to escape the heat of the city. I found the ambiance to be truly exceptional, especially with the way the sunlight filters through the space during the afternoon.
The coffee here is clearly handled with expert precision, showcasing a depth of flavor that only a dedicated roastery can achieve. Whether you prefer a bold espresso or a creamy latte, the quality of the beans shines through in every single sip. However, the true standout of the visit had to be the tiramisu, which was executed to perfection. It struck the ideal balance between the bitterness of the coffee-soaked layers and the airy sweetness of the mascarpone cream. Every bite was indulgent without being overwhelming, making it one of the best desserts I’ve had in the region. Between the scenic riverside seating and the high-end menu, it is easily a highlight of the Chiang Mai cafe scene. It is the kind of place where you can lose track of time just watching the water flow while enjoying a world-class treat. I would highly recommend this spot to anyone who appreciates great design as much as they do a professional-grade brew.

user_reviews.Description:
We have been here twice now and there are so many good things about this cafe - it is definitely in my top 2 favorite cafes in Chiang Mai!

1) FOOD: all the beverages & snacks we ate so far have been YUMMY. I esp like the soft latte (like a light latte with ice cream & whipped cream) & absolutely LOVE their scones with clotted cream & jam. The scone is a small cute little pastry, paired with a real clotted cream (like from a real tea service, not just butter.)

2) SERVICE: their staff work very quickly & efficiently to bring you what you ordered by using the tabletop number signage, there are many people working to deliver orders & clear tables, and most importantly the staff are friendly, helpful, & customer service oriented. For example, we had a little snafu or misunderstanding with our order (which was easily just as much our fault with our communication!) but they were so apologetic & accommodating in trying to make up for the misunderstanding, even when we insisted we were the ones who made a mistake while ordering! Then they tried to refund some of our money! (We did not take it & insisted they please put it in their tip box!) Lovely!

3) ATMOSPHERE: the view & ambiance are lovely - scenic water, lush trees, many indoor & outdoor areas, plus a variety of seating options- lounge chairs, couches, arm chairs, tables & chairs in a quiet room if you want a work space, etc. (Plus, many of the staff were willing to help take photos since many of their seats are scenic with a view!)

HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PLACE! 👍

* 🚕 Parking can be limited, so I would recommend taking Grab for a hassle-free visit.

If you’re serious about specialty coffee or simply want to experience one of Chiang Mai’s best cafés, Roastery Coffee is definitely worth adding to your itinerary.

Overall, it’s a charming little gelato shop that serves great flavors with a friendly vibe. Definitely recommended!

user_reviews.Name: Anc
user_reviews.Description:
The indoor area is quite small. If there's a large group of customers, you're most likely going to need to take turns playing with the cats.

And if you happen to arrive at a time when the cats are all sleeping, well, then, probably best just spend time playing some board games provided for free.

None of the cats I observed were curious with the humans, except when they're bribed with food (not kibbles laying on their regular bowls). 90% were sleeping, or hiding away at a corner. Most are ok with petting, but they mostly mind their own business and dgaf about visitors (I suppose they've grown weary of strangers and just acted naturally?)

Also, with the small space and some 10+ cats, there's bound to be a smell. Those that claim there's no smell probably have been living with cats all along, or spent more than 30+ mins inside. It's pronounced when one just steps into it and the smell will integrate with your senses once you're in it long enough. The smell is not that bad though.

The drinks are a little expensive, but they don't charge any other fees so it's reasonable.

I just found it rather boring tbh.

user_reviews.Name: liping gan
user_reviews.Description:
KLAY Café is such a beautiful hidden gem in Chiang Mai. The moment you step in, you’ll feel the calm, minimalist vibe — warm wood tones, natural textures, soft lighting, and thoughtful interior design that makes the whole space feel cozy yet modern. It’s the kind of café where you just naturally slow down and enjoy your meal.

We tried a few dishes and everything was beautifully plated and full of flavour:

Smoked Salmon & Eggs Toast
The toast was soft and buttery, topped with generous slices of fresh salmon and perfectly runny eggs. The mix of pickles, tomatoes, and passionfruit on the side added a bright, refreshing balance. Loved how satisfying yet light it was.

Thai Beef Salad
A colourful bowl with tender slices of beef, sweet oranges, juicy tomatoes, red onions, and a nice kick from fresh chili. It’s refreshing with a nice balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy — great for brunch or a hot day.

Besides the food, the café also has a small curated retail corner with skincare and lifestyle products, adding a boutique feel to the place. It’s a lovely spot for brunch, a slow afternoon coffee, or even just to chill and enjoy the aesthetic environment.

Overall, KLAY Café is definitely worth a visit if you’re in Chiang Mai — delicious food, beautiful ambience, and a very inviting atmosphere.

user_reviews.Name: Tyler
user_reviews.Description:
If you’re serious about coffee, Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store is a must-visit in Chiang Mai. This place completely lived up to the hype for us. From the moment you walk in, you can tell coffee is taken very seriously here — the space feels modern, stylish, and almost like a specialty coffee lab rather than just a café.

The coffee itself was incredible. Smooth, rich, perfectly balanced, and easily some of the best coffee we had in Thailand. You can really tell why Roast8ry has become internationally known in the coffee world, especially with their award-winning baristas and latte art. Watching the drinks being made honestly felt like part of the experience itself. (Food & Wine)

We also loved the atmosphere. The dark modern interior, the smell of freshly roasted beans, the music, and the overall energy made it somewhere we genuinely wanted to stay for a while instead of just grabbing a coffee and leaving. It felt trendy without trying too hard.

It’s located in the Nimman area which is already one of the best neighborhoods in Chiang Mai for cafés and restaurants, so it fits perfectly into a café hopping day around the city. Prices are definitely higher than local Thai coffee shops, but for the quality and experience, it was absolutely worth it.

If you enjoy specialty coffee even a little bit, Roast8ry Flagship Store is one of those places in Chiang Mai that you should not skip.

user_reviews.Name: Syrristen
user_reviews.Description:
Delicous food, great service and fantastic vibes!

The food was great. It was very well made, came quickly and tasted just like it was supposed to. Both drinks and food were very profesionally made. It was a little but pricey compared to other places, but it's a very touristy place and there's a lot of upkeep with the fish, so it's understandable.

And of course, the venue! It was so cool with all the fish, and the seats were inside of the pool, under waterlevel, so that you could easily see, feed and interact with the hundreds of fishes there. Ask for fish food and you will get 2 choices; normal fish food or a baby bottle so you can feed them like a baby.

The whole experience was really fun and I recommend you try it when you're in town 😄

You can feed the fish by purchasing fish pellets and fish milk provided by the café. One of the highlights is the uniquely designed toilet area filled with koi fish — it’s definitely something you should check out when you visit.

Hopefully, the management can look into improving this issue, as the café has great potential with its creative concept and design.

The Carp Café in Chiang Mai is definitely worth a visit. The atmosphere is really unique and makes it a great place for a relaxed lunch or dinner. 🐟🌿

The whole place is surrounded by countless koi carp, some of them absolutely huge, swimming right around the seating areas. The café itself shows a little bit of age in a few places, but that really doesn’t matter – you come here for the experience, and that is fantastic.

The food was also very good, and the prices were surprisingly reasonable. I honestly expected it to be much more expensive considering how special the setting is.

If you visit with children, definitely buy some fish food for 20 baht – or even better, get one of the feeding bottles for 40 baht. 😄 Feeding the koi with the bottle was a huge hit with the kids and a lot of fun.

Funny enough, it’s even cheaper than doing something similar at Chiang Mai Zoo.

Great atmosphere, good food, fair prices and a really fun experience. Clear recommendation! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

user_reviews.Name: Eugene Bogdanov
user_reviews.Description:
One of the most memorable specialty coffee experiences I've had.
I ordered a V60 brewed with locally grown Thai beans from Chiang Rai. The coffee itself was excellent—clean, sweet, well-balanced, with delicate floral and fruity notes—but what really impressed me was the attention to detail.

The coffee was served in a wine glass with a lid to preserve the aroma, alongside a handwritten brew card showing all the extraction parameters: brew ratio, dose, water temperature, brew time, TDS, and even the expected flavor profile. It felt less like ordering a cup of coffee and more like a personalized tasting experience.

You can tell the team genuinely cares about every step of the process, from sourcing the beans to the final presentation. If you enjoy specialty coffee, MoR is absolutely worth a visit.

user_reviews.Description: I stayed here for 10 nights and chose it mostly because its located at a walking distance from the Night Bazaar, the Wat Chedi Luang (a 10 to 15 min. walk to both) and because of the price - it was quite hard to find a non-shared room for less than USD 15, especially an a/c one, very much needed in Chiang Mai.||I got the Superior Room - No Balcony, but upgraded to the one with balcony for less than a couple dollars per night. They gave me a discount because I had a long stay here. Both rooms are small indeed, but I found them comfortable enough. There's a double bed with a firm-but-comfortable mattress, nice pillows and comforter, a small bedside table, cable flat screen TV, and two 0.5L complimentary bottles of water per night. The bathroom is also small but it's not cramped. The water is hot (you can adjust the temperature), the water pressure is good and the towels are big. The a/c works pretty well.||The staff is friendly and kind. Their youngest "staff, Minah, is such a pretty, well behaved and cute little girl! It's a very homey feeling you get here. They provide laundry service at 40 baht/kg and will clean the room upon request. There's indeed a lot of mosquitoes, but I suppose you can just ask for a bug spray. I managed to kill the ones in my room on the first night and didn't get any more uninvited visitors. There's no elevator here and the rooms are located on the 3rd and 4th floor. I also got a 1h foot scrub with massage for THB 350 and it was very good. The sir who did it has a very firm grip, which I prefer and not only my foot and calf are soft and smooth, but the calf pain I was feeling after so much walking is gone!||There's plenty of B&Bs and restaurants on the street where F.K. House is located to have meals. I recommend Da's Home Bakery for their Mixed fruit with Muesli and Yogurt, Addy's Happy Smoothies for their Iced Thai Milk Tea and Iced Coffee Milk, and Lucky Too for their pizzas.||Right on the corner it's Somphet Fresh Food market where, apart from fruit and vegetables, you can buy BBQed meat and fish, small trays of sliced fruits (10 to 20 baht), fruit shakes (40 baht) and some souvenirs - good to have an idea of starting prices before going to the other famous markets. Within 100m you can find a Tesco Lotus Express, a 7-Eleven, ATM, drugstores and local restaurants. I recommend Grazie Thai, I had so many meals there and the dishes are very tasty! I also tried Aroy Dee but for me it was just okay.||For the price, comfort, and location, I'd say it's a great deal!

Nestled on the top floor of the building, away from the bustling streets of Nimman, is FOHHIDE. They have a good variety of coffee drinks and mixes, which is nice, but what the place truly delivers is the experience that comes with it.

The view looks directly towards Doi Suthep, over the rooftops of Nimman, with planes flying by; all from the comfort of an air-conditioned café. In fact, on a good day where clouds are thinner, you may even spot Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.

Best of all, they accept Apple Pay/card and mobile payments without any extra charge (as I write this), and the coffee is pretty well priced. I found myself coming back multiple times over the next few days.

user_reviews.Name: Koravit Thummanond
user_reviews.Description:
Lot of Taste, better known as L.O.T., is a specialty coffee café in Chiang Mai's Nimman area. Designed with a minimalist blend of exposed concrete and warm wood, the space feels open, bright, and relaxing thanks to the abundance of natural light. Rather than being a café built purely for Instagram, it is a place where people come to enjoy good coffee. One of its highlights is the variety of coffee beans available, along with its signature drinks featuring Soft Cream, which gives the café a unique identity beyond a typical latte.

When I visited, the café was quite busy with a mix of locals, tourists, and expats. Some were working on their laptops while others were catching up with friends, yet the atmosphere remained calm and comfortable.

Here's what I tried:

Hot Latte
The café uses its own house blend, combining beans from Doi Chang and Lator Gold. The result is a balanced cup with smooth milk, gentle acidity, low bitterness, a creamy texture, and subtle caramel sweetness. It's easy to drink and well-rounded without being overpowering.

Soft Latte
This is the café's signature drink and one that many people come specifically to try. Instead of traditional milk foam, it's topped with a thick layer of Soft Cream, similar in texture to soft serve, sitting on an iced latte. Each spoonful gives you both coffee and cream together. The Soft Cream is silky and lightly sweet—lighter than whipped cream and far less sugary than ice cream. It's worth tasting the cream on its own first before gently stirring it into the coffee, as the flavor gradually changes from the first sip to the last.

Tiramisu
The tiramisu has a light, airy texture with just the right amount of sweetness. It pairs naturally with coffee without feeling too rich, and melts smoothly in your mouth.

If you're exploring Nimman and looking for a comfortable place to relax with a well-made cup of coffee and a slice of dessert, Lot of Taste is definitely a café worth adding to your list.

Lot of Taste Coffee, Chiang Mai

Visited this lovely café at One Nimman and had a great experience! Here are my thoughts:

* 📍 Located in the heart of One Nimman, making it a very convenient stop while exploring the area.

* 🚕 I’d recommend taking Grab, as parking around One Nimman can be busy.

A wonderful specialty coffee spot with excellent coffee, welcoming service, and a peaceful atmosphere. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Chiang Mai!

user_reviews.Description:
This is my favorite little “hidden gem” coffee shop in Chiang Mai. Super-friendly owners, amazing coffee and non-coffee drinks (their Thai iced tea was one of the best I had in Thailand), and some tasty pastries to go along with it!  They sell some fantastic local beans as well, which I can highly recommend. For the quality, it’s amazing how reasonable the prices are.

When the weather is moderate they open up the front of the shop to be open-air, but during the heat of the afternoon they close it to keep it nice and cool inside with air conditioning. Very convenient location to grab-and-go, but they have a surprising large amount of seating for such a tiny little place: 2-3 benches/tables inside, as well as 3 tables outside. Really recommend for a getting a drink and people-watching for a wee bit outside.

Edit (August 2025): Was back in Chiang Mai and wanted to stop in again. The shop has changed a bit and become better!
